title: Tang and Song China
objective: After this level you can describe inventions of medieval China, from printing to gunpowder.
summary: Tang and Song China invented printing (the Diamond Sutra, 868; Bi Sheng's clay type), used gunpowder in fireworks, improved compasses and pioneered paper money.

cards.headline: Printing, gunpowder, the compass: a famous thinker said they changed the world.
cards.body: The English philosopher Francis Bacon never realized that all three came from China. Meet the two dynasties behind them: the Tang (618–907) and the Song (960–1279).

cards.headline: Printing, one block at a time
cards.body: Printing was invented under the Tang, first to spread Buddhist scriptures and later calendars and dictionaries. Printers carved a whole page of text into a single wooden block. The Diamond Sutra, printed in 868, is the first known dated printed book. Around 1041–48 Bi Sheng went further, with movable type of baked clay, though China didn’t follow it up. One block per page is slow; one piece per character is clever.

mascot.line: Hold on to the woodblock. Europe’s own printing press arrives in Level 91.

cards.headline: Sparks and a needle
cards.body: Gunpowder, a mix of saltpetre, sulfur and charcoal, originated in China, where people used it in fireworks and signals by the 10th century. Under the Song, advances in compasses, charts and instruments helped ships trade over long distances. Its first big jobs were lighting up the sky and finding the way across the sea.

cards.headline: Money made of paper
cards.body: The Song pioneered paper money as legal tender, which helped a booming commercial economy. Several Song cities had populations of more than 1,000,000. Remember Level 65, where paper started out wrapping medicine? Under the Song it had become money itself. Quite a promotion.

cards.headline: Tang and Song China: known
learned: Printing was invented under the Tang
The Diamond Sutra (868) is the first dated printed book
Bi Sheng made clay movable type
Gunpowder lit fireworks and signals by the 10th century

questions.prompt: What is the Diamond Sutra, printed in China in 868, famous as?

options.label: The first book set in movable type
options.rationale: Bi Sheng’s clay type came later.

options.label: The first known dated printed book
The first Chinese paper banknote
options.rationale: Paper money came under the Song.

options.label: The oldest map of the Silk Road

questions.explanation: The Diamond Sutra of 868 is the first known dated printed book.

questions.prompt: By the 10th century, what were people in China using gunpowder for?

options.label: Whitening paper for printing
options.rationale: Gunpowder had nothing to do with paper.

questions.explanation: Gunpowder originated in China, where it was used in fireworks and signals by the 10th century.

questions.prompt: Level 7’s monks copied every book by hand. How did Tang printers make a page?

options.label: They carved each page into one wooden block
They cast each character separately in baked clay
options.rationale: Bi Sheng tried clay type later, but China didn’t follow it up.

options.label: They set reusable metal letters in lines
They copied it by hand in a scriptorium
options.rationale: That was the monks’ way, not the printers’.

questions.explanation: Tang printers carved a whole page of text into a single wooden block, while monks wrote out every copy by hand.
